quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #14
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Where are a truck's blind spots?

options.text: On the left side of the cab.
On the left side of the cab and directly behind the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left side of the cab and directly behind the truck.
questions.explanation: Trucks have much larger blind spots than cars. The truck driver cannot see vehicles behind them. You cannot see traffic ahead if you drive too close behind a truck. If the truck driver cannot see your car in their mirror, they cannot see you.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: Side mirrors eliminate blind spots completely.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
You can see all blind spots in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Large trucks have larger blind spots than other vehicles, and other drivers should avoid these areas.

questions.question: When making a left turn, you should not:
questions.explanation: When turning left, slow down and use your turn signal. Do not cut the corner short, as this can interfere with traffic.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Pedestrians are walking along the road ahead.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign tells drivers that pedestrians may be crossing ahead. You must stop and stay stopped until pedestrians finish crossing.

questions.question: In heavy fog, you should slow down and:
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off moisture and create glare, making it harder to see. Some vehicles have fog lights that work with low beams.

questions.question: If a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle:

options.text: Expect the child to have full control of the bicycle.

questions.explanation: Children on bicycles can be unpredictable and make sudden direction changes. Children and bicycles are small and hard to see.

questions.question: You may legally block an intersection:

options.text: If you entered the intersection on a green light.

questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection unless you can drive all the way across before the light turns red. Blocking an intersection is illegal and you can be cited.

questions.question: Driving slower than other traffic is:

options.text: A good idea in bad weather.
Okay if you don't know the speed limit.
Often dangerous because drivers may pass you unsafely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often dangerous because drivers may pass you unsafely.
questions.explanation: Driving slower than other traffic is dangerous. Impatient drivers behind you may take risky chances to pass you.

questions.question: Which factor affects how fast a person absorbs alcohol?
questions.explanation: Weight, biological sex, food in your stomach, and number of drinks affect how fast you absorb alcohol. The only way to remove alcohol is to wait.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They warn drivers of situations ahead. This sign warns of a steep hill. Slow down to avoid collisions and brake damage.

questions.question: When turning left, a driver must yield to:
questions.explanation: A driver turning left must yield to cars driving straight toward them. You can only turn when it is safe and the oncoming traffic is not affected.

questions.question: Traffic control devices in work zones are what color?
questions.explanation: Orange signs, cones, and barriers are used in work zones. Drive carefully when you see orange warning signs.

questions.question: Extra space in front of a large truck is needed so:

options.text: Other drivers can merge onto the freeway.
The truck driver has room to stop.
Other drivers have room to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck driver has room to stop.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more distance to stop than cars traveling at the same speed. Do not pull in front of a truck and then slow down or stop.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Look over your shoulder toward the lane you plan to move into.
Use only the left side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder toward the lane you plan to move into.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder to check for traffic in your blind spot. Check multiple times before changing lanes. Watch traffic both in front of you and in the next lane.

questions.question: During dawn, dusk, rain, or snow when visibility is low, turn on your:
questions.explanation: Use your headlights whenever you cannot see other vehicles or when other drivers cannot see you. Turn on your headlights if weather conditions require you to use your windshield wipers.

questions.question: When you have a green light and pedestrians are in the intersection, you must:

options.text: You have the right to cross before pedestrians.

questions.explanation: Even with a green light, you must yield to pedestrians and other vehicles already in the intersection. When turning on a green light, yield to pedestrians.

questions.question: When entering or leaving a driveway, drivers should:

options.text: Honk at pedestrians to make them move faster.

questions.explanation: When crossing a sidewalk to enter or leave a driveway, parking lot, or alley, you must yield to pedestrians. You cannot drive on a sidewalk except to cross it.

questions.question: In rain, be extra careful when turning or stopping:

options.text: After it has rained all day.
One half hour after the rain stops.
During the first half hour of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first half hour of rain.
questions.explanation: Be most careful during the first half hour of rain. Oil from cars mixes with rain water on the pavement, making it very slippery.

questions.question: When following a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Be ready to use your horn.

questions.explanation: Keep a three to four second following distance behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop quickly. Extra distance protects both of you and gives you room to avoid the rider if they fall. The risk of falling is highest on wet roads, gravel, and metal surfaces like bridges and railroad tracks.

questions.question: When driving behind a large truck on the freeway, you should:

options.text: Drive closer than you would behind a regular car.
Drive farther back than you would behind a regular car.
Drive to the right of the truck and wait to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive farther back than you would behind a regular car.
questions.explanation: Drive farther behind a large truck than you would behind a regular car because trucks have large blind spots.

questions.question: What do yellow lines separate?

options.text: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of a two-way road. A solid yellow line means you cannot cross it to pass. A broken yellow line means you can cross it to pass, but only if it is safe and will not interfere with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line between two lanes mean?

options.text: Both lanes of traffic are going in the same direction.
You can pass when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Dashed yellow lines separate lanes with traffic moving in opposite directions. You can pass when there is no oncoming traffic in the passing lane.

questions.question: When can you cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle?

options.text: When the vehicle in front moves to the right to let you pass.
When the yellow line next to your side of the road is broken.
When the yellow line next to the opposite side of the road is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the yellow line next to your side of the road is broken.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to your side means you can pass if it is safe to do so. A solid yellow line on your side means you cannot pass.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on snow or ice?

options.text: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
Stay close behind other vehicles to maintain traction.
Pump your brakes to keep them from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
questions.explanation: Shift to a low gear before going down a steep hill to prevent skidding. Also, stay farther back from the vehicle ahead than normal. Avoid quick stops. If you don't have antilock brakes, pump the brakes gently to slow down or stop.

questions.question: How can any amount of alcohol affect a driver?

options.text: It affects your judgment and physical coordination.

questions.correctAnswerText: It affects your judgment and physical coordination.
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol can impair your ability to drive safely. Any alcohol can affect your judgment and coordination, even if the amount is below the legal limit. Driving after drinking any amount of alcohol can result in criminal charges.
